linkedin.title: Most news apps are built to keep you scrolling until you are exhausted.
linkedin.body:
That is the default model for the internet. It relies on outrage, endless notifications, and the assumption that your attention is a resource to be mined. We wanted to build something different.

At Headlinne, our philosophy is simple. We believe news should be helpful, not overwhelming. We use AI not to feed you more content, but to filter out the noise. The goal is to give you exactly what you need to understand the world, and then let you get on with your day.

True intelligence in a news app means respecting your time. It means surfacing the facts without the fluff. It means removing the incentives to click and replacing them with the incentives to learn. A smarter news experience isn't about knowing everything. It is about knowing what matters to you.

instagram.title: Canada Supreme Court upholds Quebec religious symbol ban

slides.headline: Canada Supreme Court upholds Quebec religious symbol ban
slides.subtitle: The law restricts religious attire for public servants.

slides.explanation: This decision impacts a wide range of public employees across Quebec. It effectively changes the dress code for teachers, police officers, and lawyers.

slides.headline: The law prioritizes secularism over some individual rights
slides.explanation: While the government argues this protects a secular society, critics say it weakens legal protections for fundamental rights by targeting specific religious expressions.
We compared reports from Deutsche Welle and the Guardian. While they differ on specific counts, both confirm the court's decision to uphold the bill.

slides.subtitle: Read the full breakdown on Headlinne.

instagram.caption:
Quebec's Bill 21 has been a point of intense debate for years.

The law prohibits public servants in positions of authority from wearing religious symbols while on the job.

Now, the Supreme Court has largely upheld the legislation. Supporters see this as a necessary step to maintain a secular state, while opponents argue it unfairly infringes on personal freedoms.

This ruling settles a significant legal chapter in Canadian constitutional law. It highlights the ongoing tension between provincial autonomy and federal human rights standards.

story_card.headline: Hackers are using AI to automate cyberattacks
story_card.standfirst: Microsoft warns that state-backed groups are using new AI tools to speed up system

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Hackers in China and North Korea are using an AI tool called ARTEX to infiltrate tech systems.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: This framework automates common attack techniques that humans used to perform manually.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: The automation is so efficient that it can potentially bypass weak defenses in just minutes.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Security teams will need to update their defenses to counter these faster, automated threats.

story_card.caption:
Microsoft has identified state-backed hackers using the ARTEX AI tool for cyberattacks.

The report highlights an 'agentic offensive framework' that allows attackers to scale their efforts. By automating familiar techniques, these groups can find and exploit vulnerabilities much faster than before.
